title: Prove Cursor turns in Node Vitest

intentCoverage.report:
Dough Intent Coverage — SEED-413#prove-cursor-turns-on-vitest

Verdict: Caught.

Story and revision: .planning/seeds/SEED-413-renovate-dashboard-unit-tests.md#prove-cursor-turns-on-vitest, plan .planning/slice-plans/872-prove-cursor-turns-on-vitest/PLAN.md, probed at aa6ee4483c067e5ab32541ab8e76a7e4e9968c1f (implementation tip cb5183f27564dab82eacf4a91c0d234957cc974d is an ancestor of that revision).

Promise: an instructed Cursor launch writes the instruction only when the screen is ready. A trust prompt that never becomes the composer does not receive it, and the first input stays uncertain (story Scope bullet 1 and Key example 1).

Fault (revised from the suggestion): dashboard/server/hosts/cursor/instructionDelivery.ts only holds the timeout explanation text, so it is not a readiness gate. The launch readiness gate is cursorReady in dashboard/server/hosts/cursor/terminal.ts. Runner keep (runnerKeep.ts) passes it as `ready` to attachments.keep and confirms the first input through onEntered. The single change was `return showsFollowUpLine(screen);` to `return showsFollowUpLine(screen) || showsCursorWorkspaceTrust(screen);` (plus the import from ./workspaceTrust.ts). That treats Cursor's workspace trust prompt as ready. No fixtures or assertions were changed.

Focused command (as suggested, unchanged): npm run test:dashboard:backend -- 'terminals/agent-terminal-cursor-launch\.spec\.ts$' --workers=1, run in an isolated scratch git worktree at /tmp/intent-cov-872 (detached at aa6ee448, npm ci, clean pre-probe git status).

Run observations:
- Baseline: 6 of 6 passed, including "a trust prompt that never becomes the composer does not receive the instruction" (:149) and "a screen that is not ready receives the instruction when it becomes ready" (:181). This confirms the checks ran.
- Faulted: 2 failed, 4 passed (exit 1). Both failures are at the assertion `expect(recorded.firstInput).toMatchObject({ state: "uncertain" })`:
  - In :149 it fails at agent-terminal-cursor-launch.spec.ts:157.
  - In :181 it fails at line 192.
  - Both report "expected { state: 'confirmed', … } to match object { state: 'uncertain' }".
  The composer, working, multiline and question cases still passed, so the fault was confined to the trust path.
- Independent wrong-behavior witness: a temporary scratch spec (terminals/zz-intent-witness.spec.ts, later deleted) used installFakeCursor({ screen: "trust" }) with withInstructedCursor in boundary mode. It only logged enteredInstruction(cursor, pid), the raw PTY input and the recorded firstInput state.
  - Unfaulted: entered "", raw "", state "uncertain".
  - Faulted: the full launch instruction ("hold this launch" plus the dashboard reporting context) was written to the trust-prompt PTY and submitted with a carriage return, and the state was "confirmed".
  This establishes reach and wrong behavior on the intended path.

Catching assertion: agent-terminal-cursor-launch.spec.ts:157 `expect(recorded.firstInput).toMatchObject({ state: "uncertain" })` in "a trust prompt that never becomes the composer does not receive the instruction", with the same assertion at :192 in the become-ready case. The later `expect(enteredInstruction(cursor, pid)).not.toContain(instruction)` (:159 and :194) was not reached because the earlier state assertion failed first. The claim is limited to the trust-prompt launch path in this spec. The fault was not probed against agent-terminal-cursor-launch-wait.spec.ts or agent-terminal-cursor-trust-join.spec.ts.

Restoration: the fault was applied under a shell trap that restored the backup, and the witness file was deleted under its own trap. Post-probe `git status --porcelain` was identical to the empty pre-probe state, and `git diff --quiet` succeeded. Rerunning the same focused command passed 6 of 6 (exit 0). The scratch worktree was then removed with git worktree remove and pruned. The source checkout was never edited.

Next proof action: none required for this promise on the trust-prompt launch path. Optionally, probe the same fault against agent-terminal-cursor-launch-wait.spec.ts to cover the workspace-trust-uncertain path. No already-planned repair or prior disposition matches this evidence, and the probe makes no new repair decision.

Costs:
- Test runtime: measured, Vitest-reported Duration for each focused run. Baseline 42.60 s, faulted 38.14 s and restored 47.27 s (127.01 s total for the focused spec). The two witness runs were roughly 18 s wall-clock combined (measured, shell-reported command time for both).
- Human effort: unavailable. No human worked during this delegated probe, and no separate human time measure exists.
- Agent effort: unavailable as a separately supported measure. No token or agent-time meter is exposed to this subagent. Elapsed time below is the only measured proxy.

- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 240159 ms (measured), from 1795746358846 to 1795746599005 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

Wrap-up disposition: Checked revision aa6ee4483c067e5ab32541ab8e76a7e4e9968c1f; Verdict: Caught; no follow-up needed.
